title: Error log
intro: Errors of recordings, analyses and comparisons, newest first and kept across restarts (the last 500). Hover over or tap a message to see what happened and what to do.
confirm_clear: Clear the error log? The recordings and their status stay as they are.
generic.what: vinyl-check stopped this step with the message above.
generic.todo: Run it again (↻). If the error comes back, the service log has the details (on a Raspberry Pi: journalctl -u vinyl-check).
jobs.integrity_error.what: Before every analysis vinyl-check compares the recording's file with the checksum stored when it was first processed. They differ, so the file changed after that: usually it was damaged or replaced (a storage fault, a copy made by hand). Up to version 1.2 it also happened when a recording was analysed while it was still running (↻ during the recording): the checksum then belonged to the unfinished file, and the file itself is fine.
jobs.integrity_error.todo: The station repairs the case of an analysis during the recording by itself at its next start (version 1.3 or later). Otherwise play the recording: if it breaks off or sounds wrong, delete it and record the side again.
jobs.audio_missing.what: The recording's file is not where the database expects it: it was moved or deleted outside vinyl-check, or the drive with the user-data folder is not mounted.
jobs.audio_missing.todo: Check under System → Storage that the drive is there. If the files are in another folder, use Settings → Storage → Only relink. If they are gone, delete the recording.
jobs.audio_deleted.what: The original audio was deleted after the retention period (Settings → Retention). Measurements, grades and comparisons are kept.
jobs.audio_deleted.todo: Nothing to repair. To analyse recordings again later, keep their audio longer under Settings → Retention.
jobs.calibration_too_loud.what: The chain noise is measured with the stylus raised: the noise of the electronics alone. The level was far above that, so the stylus was probably in the groove, or loud hum reached the input.
jobs.calibration_too_loud.todo: Raise the stylus, let the platter spin and start the calibration again. If it stays too loud with the stylus up, check the ground lead and the cables (hum).
jobs.worker_crashed.what: The process that does the number crunching ended unexpectedly, most often because memory ran out.
jobs.worker_crashed.todo: Analyse the recording again (↻). If it happens again, close other programs or check the load on the System tab.
jobs.no_master.what: The master comparison needs the digital master of this side, and none is stored.
jobs.no_master.todo: Upload the master of the side on the record page (engineer mode), then start the check again.
jobs.master_file_missing.what: The master file of this side is not where the database expects it.
jobs.master_file_missing.todo: Check the drive under System → Storage, or upload the master again.
jobs.analyze_first.what: A comparison needs analysed recordings, and this one was not analysed (yet).
jobs.analyze_first.todo: Wait until the analysis has finished, or analyse the recording again (↻), then compare again.
jobs.both_analyze_first.what: A comparison needs analysed recordings, and at least one of the two was not analysed (yet).
jobs.both_analyze_first.todo: Wait until both analyses have finished, or analyse them again (↻), then compare again.
jobs.sample_rate_mismatch.what: The two recordings were made at different sample rates and cannot be aligned sample by sample.
jobs.sample_rate_mismatch.todo: Compare recordings made with the same audio settings (Settings → Audio interface).
api.recording_too_short.what: The recording ended after less than 3 seconds, too short to analyse: it was stopped right away, or the device delivered no audio.
api.recording_too_short.todo: Record the side again. If it stops at once again, test the device under Settings → Audio interface.
api.recording_interrupted.what: The station was restarted or switched off while this side was being recorded, so the file ends where it stopped.
api.recording_interrupted.todo: Record the side again. Updates wait until no recording runs; a power cut or pulling the plug does not.
audio.device_not_found.what: The recording device was not there when the recording started.
audio.device_not_found.todo: Check that it is connected and switched on, then choose it under Settings → Audio interface or in the turntable profile.
audio.device_stalled.what: The device stopped delivering audio during the recording, so the recording was ended. Typical causes: a loose USB cable, a USB hub without enough power, an interface that was switched off.
audio.device_stalled.todo: Check cable and power, then record the side again.
audio.device_busy.what: Another program uses the device with exclusive access.
audio.device_busy.todo: Close that program and start the recording again.
audio.digital_silence.what: The device delivered nothing but exact zeros: the wrong input is selected or its level is at zero.
audio.digital_silence.todo: Check the input under Settings → Audio interface and the input level in the system settings.
audio.digital_silence_mac.what: The device delivered nothing but exact zeros: macOS blocks the input until vinyl-check may use the microphone, or the wrong input is selected.
audio.digital_silence_mac.todo: Allow microphone access for vinyl-check (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone), then check the input under Settings → Audio interface.
capture.busy.what: Only one recording or level check can run at a time.
